findings.text: The readme page shows its title twice: the page title "A readme as the page" and then the same line again as the readme's own `# A readme as the page` heading (make-readme-page/sheet.png, at all three widths). Either drop the `#` line from make/readme-page/readme.md or have the page not print its own title. This is the example of the pattern, so other pages will copy the double title.

The layout hub says everything twice. core/Page/layout/page.js draws the five shapes and the nine layout links as icon sections, and then renders layout/readme.md underneath, which lists the same five shapes (as a table) and the same links again. Keep the widgets and cut the readme down to "Choosing one" plus the word-collision note, or drop the second icon section. The screenshot (layout/sheet.png) only shows the top, so the repeat sits just below the fold.

The pattern the docs teach is not the one the pages use. make/page.js:100 and make/readme-page/readme.md:6 both show `content(){ return md.file(import.meta, "readme.md"); }`, but layout/page.js:46 and make/readme-page/page.js:19 wrap it as `div().append(md.file(...))`, with a comment saying a Page cannot take the promise. Page.class.js:272 and :384 already use the plain one-liner, so it works. Use the one-liner wherever a page is only its readme, and make the comment explain that the wrapper is needed only when JS follows it.

The engine covers all seven asks. Ask 1 is the recipe (core/Page/expert.json). Ask 2 is the read-me verb (`readme`, `load_module`, `readme_modules`). Ask 3 builds a base checkpoint and forks it for each question; derived checkpoints are `build({extra, from})`. Ask 4 stores a sha1 for every file and rebuilds lazily on the next ask. Ask 5 adds the `ask_expert` and `list_experts` tools, plus the one-line addition to three skills. Ask 6 is the four-way proof table in proof.md. Ask 7 is `model`, `deep_model` and `deep:true`. The answer to the owner's "checkpoint or fresh load?" question is measured: a fork costs about $0.03 per question and a preloaded prompt about $0.38.

Servex/experts.json does not exist in the main checkout yet. So `list_experts` returns an empty list, and the first live `ask_expert core/Page` pays the one-time build (~$0.32–0.45) while the caller waits. Build the base once after the Servex restart, so the discovery index has a row in it.

Every chain readme is hashed too (Servex/agents/experts.js:136), and that includes the root readme.md and framework/readme.md. Any edit to those two files makes every expert stale and rebuilds them all. That is cheap today with only one expert. Once there are many, consider checking freshness against the recipe's `load` files only.

An `ask_expert` call can block for a long time: a rebuild can take up to 900 s and the answer up to 600 s (experts.js:229 and :273). Check that the MCP HTTP client and the fast assistant can wait that long, or return early with "rebuilding, ask again".

The build spawns with `cwd: REPO` through Agents.js, which also prepends `first_prompt(dir)` and `whoami` (Agents.js:101-103). The root readme may then reach the checkpoint twice, once there and once in the bundle's chain. Look at one built session's first message to confirm.

`record()` reads Servex/experts.json, changes it and writes it back (experts.js:188). Two builds running at once would lose a row, and memory records this read-modify-write pattern losing entries before. A rare risk while builds are this infrequent.

`.claude/settings.json` raises `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` to 150000 for every session in the repo, only so that `load_module` fits. It also means about 78k tokens land in a mastermind's main context in one call. That is heavier than the owner's "iceberg" (brief, the rest on demand), so the doc should name `ask_expert` as the default and `load_module` as the exception.
The owner's side request for a minion to explore full-width summary/accordion styles (owner-words.md, 3:45 PM) is not in requirements.md or this diff. Check that it was routed somewhere.

Space is poorly used: the new pages sit in a column about 600–720px wide, leaving 70–85% of the screen empty at 1920 and 3440 (layout/sheet.png, make/sheet.png). This is the site's standard page width, not a regression, but the icon grids on the layout hub could spread wider. Navigation is clear: Layout (v1) and "A readme as the page" both appear in the tree under their parents.
